newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks set for record, profit taking seen later.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks set for record, profit taking seen later.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to race to record levels in early trading on Thursday, following on from a sharp increase in prices on Wednesday, but brokers said profit-taking could set in later.

The Hang Seng Index scored a record closing high on Wednesday with a rise of 292.03 points, or 1.89 percent, to 15,738.81. Brokers said it was likely to rise above its intra-day record high of 15,783.27 points on Thursday.
"Hongkong Bank was higher in London, the Dow moved to a record and locally there is no fresh news but we are expecting good earnings," said Vickers Ballas sales director Antony Mak.
He said red chip stocks seemed to have run out of steam and money should flow from the sector into the blue chips, possibly giving the Hang Seng Index a boost of about 100 points.

"I think it will open firm and then come off a bit," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities. He said the Hang Seng Index could stage a 140-point rally before profit-taking sets in.

Galbraith said Angang New Steel Co Ltd's trading debut would be the focus this morning. Analysts expect a weak performance due to the poor investor response to its Hong Kong public offering. -- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6345
